report:
Contrary to the view that dexamethasone is ineffective, strong clinical evidence demonstrates that dexamethasone significantly **reduces mortality** and improves survival rates in critically ill COVID-19 patients. While no medical treatment guarantees survival for 100% of patients, dexamethasone is a proven, life-saving standard of care for severe cases.

### Key Evidence
* **RECOVERY Trial:** In the landmark randomized trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine*, dexamethasone (6 mg daily) reduced 28-day mortality by approximately 35% in patients on invasive mechanical ventilation and by 20% in those receiving supplemental oxygen (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436).
* **World Health Organization (WHO):** Based on aggregated clinical trial data, the WHO strongly recommends systemic corticosteroids for severe and critical COVID-19 (https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/coronaviruse/module-3-corticosteroid-therapy-and-covid19.pdf). Dexamethasone damps down excessive inflammation (cytokine storms) that causes lung damage and organ failure in late-stage disease (https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-dexamethasone).

### Important Nuances & Limitations
* **No Benefit in Mild Cases:** Dexamethasone does **not** benefit patients with mild or non-severe COVID-19 who do not require oxygen support. Administering steroids too early can suppress the immune system's natural ability to clear the virus.
* **Survival Improvement vs. Guarantee:** While dexamethasone significantly lowers the risk of death in critically ill patients, it reduces mortality risk rather than guaranteeing survival for every individual.
